As the sole Product Owner, Designer, and Engineer, I spearheaded the end-to-end delivery of a location-intelligent travel application. This project involved navigating the complexities of hybrid mobile architecture, real-time API orchestration, and cross-platform UX strategy to create a seamless digital travel companion.

1. STRATEGIC ARCHITECTURE & DEVELOPMENT

I opted for a Hybrid Mobile Architecture using the Adobe PhoneGap (Cordova) framework. This allowed for a single-codebase approach while leveraging the Cordova Plug-in Ecosystem to access native device hardware. By utilising a "Web View" container, I achieved platform-agnostic distribution without sacrificing access to critical mobile sensors like the GPS and Camera.

2. TECHNICAL CHALLENGES & SYSTEM OPTIMISATION

A primary engineering challenge was managing data persistence and performance within the constraints of a mobile WebView environment.

  • Database Synchronisation: I implemented a robust Web SQL/SQLite indexing strategy to ensure that local travel logs were retrievable in $O(1)$ time. This prevented UI "jank" when the database grew in size, ensuring smooth scrolling in the travel history view.
  • API Latency & Error Resilience: To handle the Geocoding API's "Quota Maxed" states and intermittent connectivity, I engineered a Fail-Soft Logic. The system detects a null response from the Google Cloud endpoints and prioritises cached location data or prompts a manual fallback, ensuring the app never crashes during a "dead zone."
  • Memory Management: I optimised the Cordova bridge by ensuring that the geolocation and camera plugins were only active during specific event listeners, significantly reducing the background battery drain on the Android OS.

3. CORE FUNCTIONALITY & API ORCHESTRATION

The application's technical backbone relies on asynchronous communication with multiple cloud services and persistent local storage.

  • Geospatial Intelligence: Integrated the cordova-plugin-geolocation to interface with the device's GPS hardware, capturing high-accuracy latitude and longitude coordinates.
  • Reverse Geocoding & Address Resolution: Implemented the Google Geocoding API to translate raw coordinates into readable physical addresses.
  • Persistent Data Storage: Developed a local database layer to store travel logs. Each entry captures a complex data object: coordinates, ISO timestamps, user-generated strings, and URI pointers for captured imagery.
  • Contextual Content Ingestion: * YouTube Data API: Engineered a dynamic search query that triggers based on the user’s current geofence to surface localised travel content.
    • Google Places API: Built a proximity-based discovery engine to identify and categorise nearby "Point of Interest" (POI) data.
  • UI Resilience: Utilised Bootstrap components for error handling and defensive design, ensuring the user is informed during latency or database write-cycles.

4. TECHNICAL DEMONSTRATION

These recordings showcase the live API handshakes, hardware integration, and the fluidity of the hybrid navigation stack.

5. PRODUCT OUTCOMES & EXPERTISE

i) Strategic Product Ownership

  • Architectural Decisioning: Critically assessed the trade-offs between Native (Java/Kotlin) and Hybrid (Cordova) development, prioritising time-to-market and cross-platform reach.
  • High-Fidelity UX: Designed and evaluated the app through a "Mobile-First" lens, focusing on touch-target sizing, haptic feedback triggers, and gesture-based interactions.
  • Lifecycle Management: Managed the transition from Adobe XD wireframes to a fully compiled Android package (APK).

ii) Hybrid Engineering Excellence

  • Service-Oriented Architecture: Successfully managed connectivity and web service dependencies, ensuring the app remains functional in varied network conditions.
  • Standardised Prototyping: Followed industry-standard design guidelines for cross-platform development to ensure UI consistency across different aspect ratios and DPI settings.

6. FUTURE ROADMAP

At the time of writing, I have identified several key evolutions to ensure the product scales effectively with emerging mobile standards:

  • Framework Migration: Transitioning the codebase from Cordova to a modern reactive framework like React Native or Flutter to leverage improved bridge performance and smoother UI thread responsiveness.
  • Edge Computing & AI Integration: Implementing on-device machine learning to automatically categorise travel photos and suggest journal tags based on visual recognition.
  • Offline-First Synchronisation: Moving from Web SQL to a CouchDB/PouchDB architecture to enable seamless background synchronisation with a cloud backend once a stable connection is re-established.
  • Enhanced Privacy Controls: Upgrading permission handling to meet upcoming Android/iOS sandboxing standards, providing users with granular location toggles.

7. TECH STACK & CORE COMPETENCIES

  • Design & Strategy: Adobe XD (High-fidelity Prototyping), User Scenario Mapping, Heuristic Evaluation.
  • Mobile Development: PhoneGap/Cordova Framework, Android SDK Build Tools.
  • Frontend Engineering: HTML5, CSS3 (Bootstrap), JavaScript (ES6).
  • Backend & Data: RESTful API Integration, Web SQL/SQLite Database Management, JSON Data Parsing.

To design and develop a mobile app and report on the iterative process of designing and developing it. The app must revolve around a “mobile moment”. For something to qualify as a mobile moment, it should not be possible / desirable to do the same activity with a laptop / desktop computer. Appropriate mobile moments could be (but are not limited to): commuting, waking up, being in a new city, hiking, sitting in a lecture, … This requirement has two main components: design and development.

The mobile moment we will be looking at is creating a private diary or journal application which enables travellers to keep track of the various places they have visited, while also finding a range of tourist attractions nearby, making your travel experience and planning easier.
